source.title: Decoupling Safety into Orthogonal Subspace: Cost-Efficient and Performance-Preserving Alignment for Large Language Models
source.authors: Yutao Mou; Xiao-Ling Zhou; Yuxiao Luo; Shi-Kun Zhang; Wei Ye

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether varying LoRA rank changes safety behavior, a different measurement of the claim that safety behavior is localized in few parameters or ranks. It does not test the original fine-tuning or token-position claims.
record.gate_note: The paper trains models on harmful prompts paired with safe responses, so its safety gains are induced by the training objective and do not test whether harmful fine-tuning erodes safety. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-prefix bypass, or benign fine-tuning that raises harmful compliance. Figure 9 reports rank-sweep safety results; the text describes the overall rank trend but does not give exact plotted values by rank.
record.test_reason: The paper installs extra safety in already-aligned instruct models with refusal SFT and DPO, full-parameter or LoRA, trained on harmful prompts paired with safe responses. It then measures how far jailbreak ASR falls. It never measures harmful or benign fine-tuning eroding safety, per-token KL, prefill or suffix bypass, or whether an aligned model's existing safety sits in few weights or ranks. The rank sweep (Fig. 9) shows that a low-rank adapter can add refusal behaviour. That is safety induced on purpose, not a localization test of existing safety, so V5 is not tested. Qi et al. 2024 (an original) and Wei et al. 2024b are cited only in related work and theory.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that LoRA refusal-training on safety-only data is a cost-efficient, performance-preserving, plug-and-play safety patch. They attribute this to LoRA placing the safety update in a low-rank subspace nearly orthogonal to the model's intrinsic transformation space.
record.recipe_differences: Uses safety-only refusal training with LoRA and evaluates jailbreak resistance; it does not test harmful fine-tuning that removes refusal, benign-data erosion, or response-token-position effects.
record.method_sensitivity: LoRA rank: the authors report a slight effect overall, with excessively large ranks able to weaken safety improvement.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA refusal-SFT on 4K safety-only examples cuts jailbreak ASR to near zero on Qwen2.5-7B, LLaMA3.1-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen2.5-14B with small capability loss. Ranks 4-20 all work, with a 'slight' rank effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A low-rank adapter trained only on safety data suffices to add robust refusal to an instruct model without capability loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety-LoRA update subspaces are near-orthogonal to W0 (max similarity <0.1), versus >0.4 for full fine-tuning. Finance and code LoRAs show higher similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety updates learned by LoRA occupy a subspace largely orthogonal to the model's intrinsic transformation subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-parameter DPO on a safety-general mixture raised LLaMA3.1-8B WildJailbreak ASR from 18.30 to 21.15 (Table 1), while lowering ASR on the other benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixing general helpfulness data into safety DPO can leave or worsen jailbreak vulnerability on some benchmarks.

record.problems: The rank-specific safety values are presented in Figure 9 without exact numbers in the text, and uncertainty estimates are not stated. The study does not test whether particular weights are necessary for safety behavior.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 9 also plots general-capability scores at each rank; omitted because those are not safety-behavior outcomes for V5. Other safety-training comparisons and data-composition results are not tests of the claim's predicted loss of safety, since the training uses harmful prompts paired with safe responses.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning; all training uses harmful prompts with safe responses.
No benign-only fine-tuning with safety measured afterwards. Safety-general mixtures are safety training, not benign erosion tests.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks are studied as the variable. Jailbreak benchmarks are used only to evaluate safety training.
No identification, pruning or removal of the aligned model's safety-critical weights or ranks. The rank sweep concerns an added adapter.
No analysis of why existing alignment is shallow.
No training aimed at spreading safety beyond early tokens, and no token-depth evaluation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are dropped. Adding safety through an adapter does not test whether existing safety is localized in few parameters. The lifelong-alignment results (Table 2) and the 14B results (Table 5) concern safety installation as well, so no rows are needed for the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful examples make a safety-trained model comply with harmful requests.
Whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Whether compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes bypass refusal.
The study varies LoRA rank and measures safety outcomes, but does not identify or remove a small set of individual weights to test whether they are necessary for safety.
Whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow across response tokens.
Whether training spreads safety beyond early response tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

rows.subject: LLAMA3.1-8B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared LoRA rank with the number of non-negligible singular values in the update
rows.measure: Number of non-negligible singular values of ΔW
rows.note: Describes update dimensionality; it does not establish that the corresponding parameters are necessary for safety behavior.
rows.check: This is a mechanical property of LoRA: the update rank equals the LoRA rank. It says nothing about safety localization in the aligned model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LoRA rank sweep on Qwen2.5-7B-IT and LLAMA3.1-8B-IT
reader_labels.reason: The study evaluates safety behavior across ranks 4, 8, 12, 16, and 20; its text reports that rank has a slight effect overall (r1-r30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors say excessively large ranks can weaken safety improvement, so safety effectiveness is not invariant to rank; the text does not specify which plotted ranks show this (r1-r30).
